description: Negotiation Table tell corpus. One terse, data-defined posture line per stance x trust band. The player reads the trader the way the trader reads the offer. Rotation is seed-deterministic via ISeededRng. Tone: cold, exhausted, human, restrained. No modern slang, no anachronisms, no fourth-wall breaks.

hostile: The table is a formality. Their hands never leave the rifle slings.
They have already decided what they are taking. The barter is theater.
Nobody sits on your side of the table anymore.
wary: They count your people before they count your goods.
The sentries shift when you reach for your pack.
Every answer comes through gritted teeth.
neutral: They talk trade, but the perimeter crews keep drilling.
The ledger is open and the knives are not put away.
A raid is being priced somewhere behind those eyes.
warm: Old debts keep the peace, barely. The ledger stays open.
They still trade like a friend, and watch you like weather.
The greeting is warm. The exit stays covered.

hostile: Whatever you set down, they intend to keep. All of it.
They weigh your pack, not your offer.
The quartermaster's fingers drum the counter like a countdown.
wary: Their eyes do the arithmetic on everything you carry.
Goods change hands here. Fairness was never on the table.
They ask what else is in the shelter, twice.
neutral: The stall is open, but the scale is loaded.
They nod along to your terms while repositioning the guard.
Whatever you agree to, expect less back.
warm: Habit, not hunger, keeps their hands moving toward your goods.
They short you gently, almost apologetically.
Old affection buys you a smaller theft than most.

hostile: The stall shutter is down. It does not open for you.
They fold their arms and wait for you to understand.
Nothing you carry is worth the conversation.
wary: The quartermaster barely glances at your offer.
They wave you off before you finish unpacking.
Come back with more than noise, they say, and mean never.
neutral: The shutter is half-open. Not today, they say. Not to you.
They listen to the whole offer, then shake their heads once.
The door stays closed, but they let you finish your sentence.
warm: They refuse softly, saving you the humiliation of arguing.
Not the goods, they say. The timing. Come back after the thaw.
They pour you something warm and trade nothing at all.

hostile: They keep their goods close and leave little space between you.
One hand stays beneath the table while they study the offer.
Their attention keeps drifting from your hands to the doorway.
They count their goods twice and yours a third time.
Nothing leaves their side of the table before the terms settle.
Their shoulders stay high, as if expecting the trade to turn.
They barely look at the goods before looking back at you.
The scale is pulled closer to them after every adjustment.
They stand instead of sitting, coat still fastened for departure.
Their jaw tightens whenever your hand moves toward the pile.
They push rejected goods back without bothering to straighten them.
The trader keeps the exit clear behind their own shoulder.
Their gaze settles on your pack longer than on the offer.
They wait through the silence without giving you anything back.
A thumb rests near the holster, never quite touching it.
wary: They turn each item over before placing it back down.
Their body stays half-turned, though they have not stepped away.
They watch the scale settle before answering with a small nod.
Their fingers stop drumming only when the offer changes.
They separate the better goods from the rest without explanation.
The trader studies your face after checking every marked price.
They lean closer to inspect, then return to the same distance.
Their hands hover over the goods without claiming them yet.
They recount one bundle quietly before considering the next.
The offer earns attention, but not enough to loosen their posture.
They glance toward their companions before moving anything forward.
A slow breath leaves them when the terms improve.
They keep one elbow on the table and both feet ready.
Their gaze softens briefly, then returns to the scale.
They wait for you to move first after each adjustment.
neutral: They set both hands on the table and wait.
Each item gets the same brief inspection before they look up.
The trader checks the scale once and leaves it alone.
Their expression barely changes as the piles shift between you.
They keep an even distance from both sides of the offer.
A steady gaze follows the numbers without lingering on your face.
They straighten one bundle while waiting for your next move.
Nothing in their posture hurries the exchange or delays it.
They listen without interrupting, then look back to the goods.
The trader rests their hands beside the scale, palms down.
They make room for another item without encouraging you to add it.
Their attention stays on the trade rather than the room around it.
They acknowledge the adjustment with a short, unreadable nod.
The goods are handled carefully, but without any visible attachment.
They wait in practiced silence for the offer to settle.
warm: Their shoulders loosen before they look over the new offer.
They leave the better goods within easy reach of your side.
The trader meets your eyes without checking the doorway afterward.
They stop recounting their pile once the terms begin to settle.
One corner of their mouth lifts, then the expression is gone.
They lean closer to the table instead of guarding their distance.
Their hands stay open while you rearrange the offer.
They nod once before checking the final weight on the scale.
The trader turns an item toward you to show its better side.
They let a silence pass without treating it as a challenge.
Their coat hangs open now, hands occupied with the goods.
They slide one bundle forward before you finish arranging yours.
Their attention stays with you even when someone passes behind them.
They inspect your goods quickly, trusting the familiar parts.
The final adjustment gets a tired nod that almost feels familiar.

hostile: They trade, they talk, and none of it can be trusted twice.
The intel comes fast and cheap, like they want you gone.
Every warning they share is also a test of what you fear.
wary: The goods are fair. The information arrives in pieces.
They tell you just enough to learn what you already know.
Advice is free here. Acting on it is not.
neutral: Between items, they mention which roads are closed.
The ledger closes and the real conversation begins.
They mark the fallout drift on your map without being asked.
warm: They set the ledger aside and speak to you like kin.
You get the news before the radio does, some nights.
They warn you about the crossing two days before the convoy burns.
